If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid overestimating bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is trending upward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% in mid horizon (days 15–24) to capture momentum bias.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is consolidating, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment in early horizon (days 1–10) to dampen overconfidence.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 after a downtrend, add a 1.0–2.0% upward correction in late horizon to reflect reversal sentiment.  
If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) across 5+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2.0–3.0% in all horizons to reflect bearish drift.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, apply a 0.5–1.5% smoothing adjustment across all horizons to reduce noise amplification.
